scenes.text: Opening a bank account used to take days of paperwork. [1] Now you photograph your ID card, take a selfie, and it's verified in minutes. [2] Let's break down how KYC document scanning works.

title: KYC
Scanning
data.subtitle: How apps read and verify your ID

scenes.text: Here's the flow. [1] You photograph your ID card. [2] Vision models find the card, straighten it, and fix the lighting. [3] OCR reads the text, like your name, date of birth and ID number. [4] The app checks those details against official records, [5] and compares your selfie with the photo on the card.

data.heading: From photo to verified
nodes: Read name, date of birth, number

scenes.text: The key step is OCR, optical character recognition. [1] It turns a picture of text into real text a computer can use. [2] It finds where the text is, [3] recognises each character, even in different fonts, [4] and works out which field is which, like name, or date of birth.

data.definition: Turning a picture of text into real text a computer can use.

scenes.text: To stop fraud, the app runs extra checks. [1] Document checks, looking for signs of editing, or a fake card. [2] A face match, comparing your selfie with the ID photo, using embeddings. [3] And liveness, making sure it's really you, live, not a photo of a photo.

Here are four terms. [1] KYC, which stands for know your customer, the rules banks follow to verify identity. [2] OCR, reading text from images. [3] Face match, comparing two faces. [4] And video KYC, a live video call with an agent, used for some accounts.
So where will you see it? [1] Opening bank and trading accounts online. [2] Getting a new SIM card, or a loan in an app. [3] And wallet and fintech apps verifying their users.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think any app asking for their ID photo is safe. [2] Only share ID documents with official, trusted apps. Scammers also ask for ID photos and selfies, so never send them over chat to strangers.

data.myth: Any app asking for my ID photo is safe.
data.fact: Only share ID with official, trusted apps. Scammers ask for ID photos and selfies too.
